An attraction in Batanes. Considered the oldest surviving traditional Ivatan house in Batanes. Located in Batan Island and made of stone and lime with a cogon roof. Originally built in 1917 and maintained through periodic roof replacement.
An attraction in Batanes. An unmanned shop located in Ivana, Batanes. Operates on a self-service system based on honesty and trust. Customers record purchases and leave payment in a designated box.

An attraction in Cagayan. An 11-hectare site featuring life-sized Stations of the Cross. A known pilgrimage destination, especially during Holy Week. Offers a scenic view of the Cagayan River and is accessible by stairs.

An attraction in Cagayan. Located in the Peñablanca Protected Landscape and Seascape. One of over 300 caves in the area, with seven chambers open to visitors. Features a natural chapel inside one of its chambers.

An attraction in Isabela. Known for its red brick façade and detailed architectural design. Completed in 1805 under Dominican missionaries. Features a rare cylindrical bell tower and is recognized as a heritage structure.
An attraction in Isabela. A large representation of the traditional reclining chair (butaka). Made from materials such as narra wood and woven rattan. Symbolizes local craftsmanship in Ilagan City.
An attraction in Nueva Vizcaya. Features Baroque-inspired architectural elements. Functions as the seat of the Diocese of Bayombong.

An attraction in Nueva Vizcaya. Located within Mount Pulag National Park in the Cordillera Mountain Range. The highest peak in Luzon at 2,922 meters above sea level. Known for its "sea of clouds" and diverse flora and fauna.

An attraction in Quirino. A scenic section of the Cagayan River with limestone formations. Known for activities such as rafting, kayaking, and swimming. Considered a major ecotourism attraction in the province.
An attraction in Quirino. A designated outdoor area for motocross and trail riding. Serves as the main venue for the Quirino Motorismo Festival. Attracts riders from different parts of the country.
A food and delicacy of Batanes. A traditional Ivatan dish made from grated banana pith and fish or meat. Known for its simple preparation and use of locally available ingredients.
A food and delicacy of Cagayan. A noodle dish topped with sautéed meat, vegetables, and egg. Served with a savory broth and known for its rich flavor.
A food and delicacy of Isabela. A roasted sheep dish known for its tender meat and crispy skin. Often served during special occasions and local celebrations.
A food and delicacy of Nueva Vizcaya. Exotic food option in the province.
A food and delicacy of Quirino. A savory dish made from pork, liver, and vegetables cooked in vinegar and soy sauce. Known for its slightly tangy and salty flavor.

A festival of Batanes. Celebrated every June 19 to July 1, this festival highlights the unique practice of the Ivatan people of voluntary work and a strong sense of community. Bayanihan is given emphasis during this event. The celebration includes cultural presentations, local games, and social gatherings.

A festival of Cagayan. Held every May 10, this festival is a thanksgiving celebration in honor of St. Peter Thelmo, the patron saint of the community. It is widely known for its boat races along the Cagayan River, participated in by local fishermen.

A festival of Isabela. Celebrated every April 20 to 23, this festival is a thanksgiving for the city's agricultural abundance. It highlights the contributions of farmers to the community and showcases the cultural diversity within the province.

A festival of Nueva Vizcaya. Held annually every August, this festival celebrates the bountiful harvest of citrus fruits in the province. The event features agricultural exhibits, fruit displays, and competitions. It aims to promote local produce, support farmers, and boost tourism.

A festival of Quirino. Known as the only motorbiking festival in the country, this event is held every July. Participants from different parts of the country join motocross races, trail rides, and other riding activities. It also highlights the natural terrain of the province.

sets.name: Region 3 - Central Luzon
sets.description: The provinces and capitals of Central Luzon, with its attractions, foods and delicacies, and festivals.

terms.term: 7 Provinces of Region 3 and Their Capitals

terms.definition: An attraction in Aurora. Located in Baler and served as the rest house of a former Philippine President. The structure is made of concrete, wood, and nipa, reflecting a simple lifestyle. Displays photographs, antique kitchenware, and preserved personal items.

An attraction in Aurora. Built in the 18th century. Known for a historic siege involving Spanish soldiers, where 54 Spanish soldiers continued to defend it even after the Spanish-American War had ended.
An attraction in Aurora. Home to a tree believed to be over 600 years old, considered one of the largest of its kind in Asia. Its trunk is so large that around 60 people are needed to encircle it.

An attraction in Bataan. A heritage resort featuring Spanish-Filipino colonial houses. The houses were transferred from different parts of the country and restored. It is the first heritage hotel in the Philippines.
An attraction in Bataan. Located on Mt. Samat in Pilar. Dedicated to Filipino and American soldiers of World War II. Serves as a historical monument.

An attraction in Bulacan. Known as the "Cradle of Democracy in the East". Site of the First Philippine Congress in 1898. Site where the Malolos Constitution was drafted and the First Philippine Republic was inaugurated.
An attraction in Bulacan. One of the largest indoor venues in the world. Has a seating capacity of more than 50,000. Used for concerts, sports events, and large gatherings.
An attraction in Nueva Ecija. A protected natural area. Known for its clear emerald river. Surrounded by high limestone cliffs.
An attraction in Nueva Ecija. Well-preserved historical residences. Reflect Spanish and early American architectural influences. Feature wooden structures and capiz shell windows.
An attraction in Pampanga. One of the oldest churches in the province. Partially buried by lahar during the 1991 Mt. Pinatubo eruption. Known as the "half-buried church".
An attraction in Pampanga. Built in 1903 during the establishment of Fort Stotsenburg. Originally used as officers' quarters. Considered among the earliest structures in the area.
An attraction in Pampanga. Formed after the 1991 eruption of a volcano, one of the largest eruptions of the 20th century. Features scenic waters at the volcano's summit.
An attraction in Tarlac. Features a 70-meter tall black monument. Honors Filipino and American soldiers. Located at the end site of the Bataan Death March.
An attraction in Tarlac. Located on a mountain in San Jose. A known religious site. Houses a relic believed to be part of the Holy Cross.
An attraction in Zambales. A museum dedicated to a former Philippine President. Displays personal belongings and memorabilia. Highlights his leadership and public service.
An attraction in Zambales. Known for its ash-colored sand and calm waters. Surrounded by agoho trees. Formed after the eruption of Mt. Pinatubo.
A delicacy of Aurora. A salad made from edible fern leaves mixed with tomatoes and onions. Known for its fresh taste and simple preparation.
A delicacy of Bataan. Made from taro root. Known for its creamy texture and natural sweetness.
A delicacy of Bulacan. A sweet cured ham commonly served during celebrations. Known for its rich and festive flavor.
A delicacy of Nueva Ecija. A sweet and garlicky beef sausage, distinct from other pork varieties.
A delicacy of Pampanga. Made from chopped pork, onions, and seasonings. Known for its savory, tangy, and slightly spicy taste.
A delicacy of Tarlac. A grilled rice cake made from glutinous rice and coconut. Wrapped in banana leaves and has a smoky flavor.
A delicacy of Zambales. Known for its sweet and juicy flavor. One of the main agricultural products of the province.

A festival of Aurora held on August 24-25. Celebrated in San Luis to highlight a local plant used in weaving mats, hats, and handicrafts. The festival includes street dancing, exhibits, and trade fairs. It showcases the skills of local artisans and promotes local livelihood. The event also supports cultural preservation.

A festival of Bataan held on the last week of November, usually November 29-30. Celebrated in Morong to promote the protection of endangered sea turtles. Activities include turtle release, coastal clean-ups, and awareness campaigns. The festival highlights marine conservation. It also encourages sustainable tourism practices.

A festival of Bulacan held on May 17-19. A religious festival where devotees dance in honor of patron saints while praying for fertility and blessings. The tradition combines Catholic practices and local beliefs. Participants perform ritual dances in the streets. The festival attracts pilgrims from different places.

A festival of Nueva Ecija celebrated every May. A traditional theatrical presentation about the search for the Holy Cross. It includes music, dance, and dialogue influenced by Spanish traditions. The event reflects strong religious faith. It remains an important cultural practice in the province.

A festival of Pampanga held on the Saturday before Christmas Day in December. Held in San Fernando and known for giant illuminated displays with moving lights. The displays feature detailed designs and vibrant colors. The festival highlights Filipino creativity. It is a major Christmas attraction.

A festival of Tarlac held on the first week of December. Showcases nativity scenes displayed in homes and public places. The festival promotes faith, family, and creativity. Communities create artistic displays. It is an important Christmas tradition in the province.

A festival of Zambales held in April, usually the 3rd week. Celebrates the mango harvest in the province. Activities include street dancing, exhibits, and trade fairs. The festival highlights the importance of mango production. It also promotes tourism and local products.

sets.name: Region 4A - CALABARZON
sets.description: The provinces and capitals of CALABARZON, with its attractions, foods and delicacies, and festivals.

terms.term: 5 Provinces of Region 4A and Their Capitals

terms.definition: An attraction in Cavite. Site where Philippine independence was declared on June 12, 1898. Former residence of the first Philippine President. Preserved as a national shrine and venue for Independence Day ceremonies.

An attraction in Cavite. Strategic military defense site during World War II. Fortified by Spanish and American forces before the Japanese occupation. Features war ruins, tunnels, and memorials open for historical tours.
An attraction in Laguna. Built in 1845 with a chapel and underground burial chamber. Used as a secret meeting place during the Philippine Revolution. Declared a National Historical Landmark in 1973.
The largest freshwater lake in the Philippines. Supports fishing, agriculture, and local livelihoods. Drains into the Pasig River and contributes to regional ecology.

terms.term: Basilica of St. Martin de Tours
terms.definition: An attraction in Batangas. Considered the largest Catholic church in Asia. Features massive Baroque architecture and Spanish-era design. Houses a notable silver tabernacle and serves as a pilgrimage site.

An attraction in Batangas. Protected mangrove area locally known as "Ang Pulo". Features walkways, viewing decks, and eco-tourism activities. Promotes environmental conservation and coastal protection.
An attraction in Rizal. The oldest known artworks in the Philippines, discovered in 1965. Features ancient carvings etched on rock surfaces. Recognized as an important cultural and historical site.

An attraction in Rizal. Conservation area known for limestone formations and forest landscapes. Offers guided trails focused on adventure and environmental education. Promotes sustainable tourism and ecological preservation.
An attraction in Quezon. Religious site featuring a large statue of the Ascending Christ. Includes pilgrimage steps, prayer areas, and biblical displays.

An attraction in Quezon. A private luxury island resort in the province. Known for white-sand beaches and well-preserved natural surroundings. Features themed villages inspired by international destinations.
A delicacy of Cavite. A noodle dish flavored with squid ink, giving it a distinct dark color and savory taste.
A delicacy of Laguna. A sweet, sticky rice delicacy layered with coconut cream, often served warm.
A delicacy of Batangas. A sweet and savory cured beef specialty from one of the province's historic towns.
A delicacy of Rizal. A fritter made from shrimp and vegetables, fried until crispy.
A delicacy of Quezon. A noodle dish eaten without utensils, traditionally served on banana leaves.
A delicacy of Quezon. A meatloaf dish cooked in llaneras, similar to embutido.

A festival of Cavite held on June 12. Celebrated in Kawit to commemorate Philippine independence in 1898. Features flag-raising ceremonies, parades, and cultural performances. Includes historical reenactments of significant events. Promotes patriotism and national pride.

A festival of Laguna held on May 15. Celebrated in Liliw in honor of the town's founding and its founder. Highlights the footwear industry through trade fairs and exhibits. Includes street dancing and cultural presentations.

A festival of Batangas held usually on May 9. Celebrates a fish found in Taal Lake. Features cooking contests, food fairs, and cultural shows. Promotes local fishing traditions and livelihoods. Encourages tourism and community participation.

A festival of Rizal held on November 23. Known for giant papier-mâché figures paraded in Angono. Celebrated in honor of San Clemente, patron saint of fishermen. Showcases creativity, artistry, and humor. Highlights Angono as the Art Capital of the Philippines.

A festival of Quezon held on May 15. Celebrated in Lucban to honor San Isidro Labrador. Houses are decorated with colorful kiping and agricultural products. Serves as a thanksgiving for a bountiful harvest. Known for vibrant and creative street displays.

folder.name: Physical Activities towards Health and Fitness

sets.name: Fitness
sets.description: The five basic principles of fitness (overload, FITT, specificity, rest and recovery, use or lose), and dynamic, static, and PNF stretching with their benefits.

terms.definition: Means that the body will adapt to the workload placed upon it. The more you do, the more you will be capable of doing. This is how all the fitness improvements occur when exercising and training. When you are working out, you want to strive to increase the workload you are doing above what you did on your previous workout so you have overloaded your body to create a training adaptation.

An easy way to get started on developing a personal fitness program. This acronym stands for Frequency, Intensity, Time and Type. These are the areas in which someone could increase or overload in order to improve physical fitness.

terms.term: The 4 Components of the FITT Principle

terms.definition: In the FITT Principle, this refers to how often you will exercise.
In the FITT Principle, this is defined as the amount of effort or work that must be completed in a specific exercise.
In the FITT Principle, this is simply how long each individual session should last. This will vary based on the intensity and type.
In the FITT Principle, this asks what type of exercise you will be doing, and what specific exercises you will perform.

terms.term: Applying FITT to Strength vs. Cardio Training
terms.definition: For Resistance/Strength Training: Frequency means increase the number of workout days; Intensity means increase the resistance/weight; Time means increase time involved in exercise or increased repetitions; Type means perform a different exercise for the same muscle group. For Cardiovascular Training: Frequency means increase the number of workout days; Intensity means increase pace for a given time or distance, or % of max heart rate; Time means increase time involved in exercise, increase the length; Type means perform a different type of exercise, e.g. running to cycling.

How you exercise should be specific to your goals. For example, if your main goal is simply health, fitness and weight management, you should focus on total body strength, cardio and a healthy diet. Make sure your training matches your goals.

Rest and recovery is also essential for reaching your weight loss and fitness goals. While you can often do cardio every day you should have at least a day of rest between strength training workouts. Make sure you don't work the same muscles two days in a row to give your body the time it needs to rest and recover.

Implies that when it comes to fitness, you "use it or lose it." This simply means that your muscles build strength (hypertrophy) with use and lose strength (atrophy) with lack of use. This also explains why we lose fitness when we stop exercising. Be consistent.
A type of exercise that improves flexibility and mobility by lengthening the muscles. Stretching is a must, not just for athletes but for anyone who wants to feel good (less pain) in life.

Involves moving parts of your body and gradually increasing reach and speed of movement. Dynamic stretches aim to get the body moving and prepared for exercise. It is for warming up before an active workout or any physical activity. Some Examples: Walking lunges, high knees, butt kicks, leg swings, arm circles, and torso twists.

Involves holding a stretch at its end range for a period of time. It is best done when your muscles are warm, like after a workout, when performed as part of a post-exercise cooldown. It can improve flexibility and decrease tension. It can also increase range of motion and improve posture. Some Examples: Hamstring stretch, quadriceps stretch, overhead triceps stretch, shoulder stretch, and child pose.

A more advanced type of stretch, typically performed with the help of a partner. It alternates between contracting and relaxing a muscle to deepen range of motion. Some Examples: Hamstring stretch, quadriceps stretch, overhead triceps stretch, and child pose (with partner).

Dynamic stretching (moving safely through a joint's full range of motion) warms up muscles and boosts power. Static stretching (holding a position for 15-60 seconds) lengthens tight muscles and promotes relaxation. Use dynamic stretches before workouts to improve performance. Use static stretches after exercise to cool down and aid recovery.
Like an engine warming up in a car, dynamic movements increase blood flow and raise your muscle temperature, making them less prone to injury.
It wakes up your nervous system so your brain and muscles communicate better for tasks involving agility and coordination.
Movements like walking lunges, high knees, or leg swings can improve your power, vertical jump, and running speed.
It lubricates your joints with synovial fluid, allowing for smoother and more fluid movement.
Holding these stretches over time permanently lengthens the muscle-tendon unit.
After a hard workout, muscles shorten and tighten. Static stretches help them relax and return to their normal resting state.
By lowering your heart rate and easing tension, it promotes blood flow to help muscles recover faster.
Regularly stretching tight muscle groups (like the chest or hamstrings) helps align your body correctly throughout the day.

sets.name: Movement Enhancement
sets.description: Exercise vs. physical activity, the three main types of exercise (aerobic, flexibility, strength training), muscular strength and endurance, and the benefits of strength training.

terms.definition: A structured program of activity geared toward achieving or maintaining physical fitness. It is actually a sub-category of physical activity.
Any form of exercise or movement of the body that uses energy. Some of your daily life activities doing active chores around the house, yard work, walking the dog are examples.
Exercise is a form of physical activity. But physical activity does not require exercise.

Any vigorous activity that increases heart rate and respiration and raises oxygen and blood flow throughout the body while using large muscle groups of the body repetitively and rhythmically. It boosts your heart and lungs health, gives you more energy, and helps you burn calories. It is an endurance-type exercise that increases a person's heart and breathing rate over a sustained period — it means "with oxygen" for sustained endurance, i.e. continuous, repetitive movements performed at low-moderate intensity. Real-world Examples: Brisk walking, jogging, running, swimming, hiking, dancing, riding a bike, cycling, and rowing.

Involves short, intense bursts of physical activity. It means "without oxygen" for short, intense bursts of power — brief exercise done at near maximal effort. Examples: Weightlifting, sprinting, jumping rope, and High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT).

A form of physical exercise in which a specific muscle or tendon (or muscle group) is deliberately flexed or stretched to improve the muscle's felt elasticity and achieve comfortable muscle tone. The result is a feeling of increased muscle control, flexibility, and its full range of motion. It keeps your joints limber, helps you bend and twist, and lowers your chances of getting hurt. Flexibility can be tested by stretching individual muscles or by performing exercises such as the lunge or the sit and reach. Real-world Examples: Yoga, Pilates, and reaching or stretching your arms and legs.

Makes your muscles work against a resistance. It builds strong muscles, protects your bones, and makes everyday tasks like carrying groceries much easier. Real-world Examples: Lifting weights, using resistance bands, or doing bodyweight exercises like push-ups, and sit-ups.
The amount of force you can put out or the amount of weight you can lift. It's measured by how much force you can exert, and how much weight you can lift for a short period of time.

The ability of a muscle or group of muscles to perform repetitive contractions against a force for an extended period. It is how many times you can move that weight without getting exhausted (very tired).

sets.name: Nutrition
sets.description: Definition of nutrition, macronutrients and micronutrients, the role of water, and the three eating disorders.

terms.definition: The study of how the body uses nutrients in food to survive, grow, and maintain health. It refers to the intake of food that meets the nutritional needs of the body. It involves the processes of consuming, absorbing, and utilizing compounds that provide energy and regulate vital bodily functions.

terms.term: The 2 Main Categories of Dietary Nutrients

terms.definition: Nutrients the body needs in large quantities to provide energy (measured in calories) and physical building blocks.
The body's primary and most readily available source of energy. Found in foods like whole grains, fruits, and vegetables.
Crucial for building and repairing tissues, hormones, and enzymes. Sourced from meats, poultry, fish, beans, and nuts.
Dense sources of sustainable energy that insulate organs, regulate body temperature, and aid in absorbing fat-soluble vitamins.
Essential elements required in smaller amounts to protect and promote bodily functions.
Organic compounds vital for immunity, energy production, and cellular protection.
Inorganic substances (like calcium, iron, and potassium) that regulate fluid levels, build strong bones, and support muscle/nerve function.

Technically required in macronutrient quantities, it acts as a universal solvent that transports nutrients, regulates temperature, and eliminates waste. Adult men typically average around 60% body water, while adult women average around 50%.
A person will control his or her weight by means of starving himself or herself for fear of being overweight even though he or she is underweight.
A person will eat a large amount of food and then force to eliminate it from the body by means of vomiting, also called purging.
This is characterized by compulsive overeating in which a person cannot control how much he or she eats.

sets.name: Physical Education, Physical Activities & Exercises
sets.description: Definitions, legal bases and objectives of Physical Education, wellness, the health- and skill-related fitness components, safety guidelines, BMI, and the body types.

terms.definition: A course program and physiological aspect to process develop skills and knowledge through physical and mind.

It refers to an individual overall health and well-being as well as their ability to perform task and physical activities effectively and efficiently with vigour and without over fatigue and enough energy.
WHO defines it as a state of complete physical, mental and social well being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity.
It is the ability to perform daily activities efficiently and effectively without experiencing excessive fatigue.

terms.term: The 2 Legal Bases of Physical Education
answers: International Charter of Physical Education and Sports
1986 Constitution of the Republic of the Philippines

terms.term: International Charter of Physical Education and Sports
terms.definition: UNESCO, Paris, 1978. Its Article 1, together with Recommendation 1 of the Interdisciplinary Regional Meeting of Experts (UNESCO, Brisbane Australia, 1962), states that the practice is a fundamental right for all, and this right should not be treated as different in principle from the right to adequate food, shelter and medical care.

The provision of the 1986 Constitution of the Republic of the Philippines stating: "The State shall promote Physical Education and encourage sports programs league competitions, amateur sports including training for international competition to foster self-discipline, teamwork and excellence for the development of a healthy and alert citizenry." It also provides that "All educational institutions shall undertake regular sports activities throughout the country and in cooperation with athletic club and other sectors."

terms.term: The 4 General Objectives of Physical Education

terms.definition: To improve fitness, strength, endurance, flexibility, coordination, and overall body functioning. To develop motor skills and promote healthy lifestyle habits that contribute to lifelong wellness.
To help individuals develop self-confidence, self-esteem, self-discipline, and emotional stability. To provide opportunities for stress relief, expression, and the development of positive attitudes.

It is the development and maintenance of meaningful interpersonal relationships. To foster teamwork, cooperation, leadership, sportsmanship, and respect for others. It encourages effective communication and the ability to work harmoniously with diverse groups of people.

To develop critical thinking, decision-making, problem-solving, and strategic thinking skills. To increase knowledge and understanding of health, fitness, movement principles, and the value of physical activity.

It is the positive state of well-being and capability of an individual to design personal fitness programs for improving and maintaining optimum levels of health. It is a combination of many different components (mental, social, emotional, spiritual and physical) that expand one's potential to live a quality life, to work effectively and to make a significant contribution to the society. It reflects how one feels about life as well as one's ability to function effectively, and is also described as the positive component of good health.

An essential subject that promotes the holistic development of students by integrating physical activity, health education, and wellness practices to enhance their overall quality of life. It helps students improve their physical fitness, including strength, endurance, flexibility, coordination, and motor skills, while encouraging healthy lifestyle habits such as proper nutrition, regular exercise, and adequate rest. It also contributes to mental and emotional well-being by reducing stress and building self-confidence, emotional resilience, and self-esteem. Through collaborative activities, it develops important social skills such as teamwork, communication, leadership, and respect for others. Additionally, it supports cognitive and academic performance by improving concentration and memory, while fostering discipline, responsibility, perseverance, and time management. Ultimately, it instills the value of lifelong physical activity and wellness, empowering students to lead healthy, active, and productive lives.

Regular exercise and physical activity promotes strong muscles and bones. It improves respiratory, cardiovascular health and overall health. It can also help you maintain a healthy weight, reduce your risk for type 2 diabetes, heart disease, and reduce your risk for some cancers.

Through regular exercise, the individual gains: proper growth of young bones and muscles; improved ability to avoid and recover from illnesses and accidents; better posture and appearance; a minimized stress response; maintenance of proper body weight; prevention of heart ailments; improved organic functions; a delayed aging process; feeling good and younger; and the joy of participation in any recreational or sports activity.

terms.term: The 5 Health-Related Components of Physical Fitness

terms.definition: The maximum amount of force that a muscle or group of muscles can exert in a single effort. It is important for performing tasks that require lifting, pushing, or pulling. Examples: Weightlifting, push-ups, and resistance training.

The ability of muscles to perform repeated contractions or sustain a contraction over a period of time without becoming fatigued. Examples: Sit-ups, planks, cycling, and repetitive bodyweight exercises.

This refers to the ability of the heart, lungs, and blood vessels to supply oxygen to the body during prolonged physical activity. Good levels of it improve stamina and reduce the risk of cardiovascular diseases. Examples: Walking, jogging, cycling, swimming, and dancing.

Refers to the ability of joints and muscles to move through their full range of motion. Good levels of it help prevent injuries, improve posture, and enhance physical performance. Examples: Stretching exercises, yoga, gymnastics, and dynamic warm-up routines.

Refers to the proportion of fat, muscle, bone, and other tissues that make up a person's body weight. Maintaining a healthy one is important for overall health and reducing the risk of obesity-related diseases. Examples of assessment: Body Mass Index, waist circumference, and body fat percentage measurements.

terms.term: The 10 Skill-Related Components of Physical Fitness

terms.definition: Ability to continue doing something difficult for a long time without giving up or becoming exhausted.
The ability to keep going without getting tired quickly. Strength and energy needed to sustain physical effort for long period of time.
This is the ability to exert force.
The ability to maximize effort of force of body to any movement with the use of muscle.
The ability to complete a movement or task in the shortest amount of time.
The ability to combine several different movement patterns in a single distinct movement with the use of the senses, which are a combination of body and mind.
The ability to control movement in each direction or intensity.
The ability to maximize the time going from one movement to another.
The ability to control the center of gravity of your body in relation to your support base.
The ability to respond quickly; "reflexes". The time required to respond or initiate a movement because of a given stimulus.

terms.term: The 4 Benefits of Health and Wellness

terms.definition: Regular physical activity is a healthy lifestyle. Healthy lifestyles such as proper nutrition, good posture and good body mechanics can help you look at your best.
People who engage in regular activity feel better. You can resist fatigue, are less likely to be injured and can work more efficiently.
Life is more enjoyable when you engage in regular physical activity that results in physical fitness as the key to being able to do more of the things you want to do.
Fit and active person has the capacity to help or to assist other people when they needed some help.

These guidelines include procedures that help prevent accidents or injury in Physical Education classes and activities. It should be recognized that many of these require cooperation in all class activities.

terms.term: The 5 Safety Guidelines in Physical Education Classes and Activities
answers: Always participate and give the best effort in every activity
Consideration should be given first to the safety of the student
Provide a pleasant atmosphere in which the students can work out

terms.definition: It tests for weight categories that may be associated with health issues. Formula: kilograms divided by meters squared. Example: 60 ÷ 1.70² = 60 ÷ 2.89 = 20.76.
More round or soft physique, gains and stores fat more easily, loses fat slowly, naturally slow metabolism.
Naturally muscular and athletic with shoulders wider than the hips; efficient metabolism making it easy to gain muscle and lose fat.
Slender with less muscle mass, narrow shoulders and hips with respect to height, naturally fast metabolism making it difficult to gain mass.

terms.term: 3 Foundations an Effective Speech Builds On

sets.description: Globalization, World Englishes, and culturally-sensitive, bias-free language.

terms.definition: A term used to describe how trade and technology have made the world into a more connected and interdependent place; it also captures in its scope the economic and social changes that have come about as a result.
In his book English as a Global Language (2003), he asserted that English is, in fact, the global language.

terms.term: 5 General Principles for Culturally-Sensitive and Bias-Free Language

terms.definition: One form of discrimination against a person or persons of a different race.
Class discrimination; a form of prejudice against a person or people because of their social class.
A form of discrimination against other people because of their age, or assuming that older people are less physically, intellectually, or emotionally able than other age groups.
Putting the person or people first when referring to people with disabilities, focusing on the person and not the condition.

sets.name: Communication Ethics
sets.description: Communication, ethics, and the NCA principles of ethical communication.

terms.definition: The act of transferring information from one place, person or group to another.
It enhances human worth and dignity by fostering truthfulness, fairness, responsibility, personal integrity, and respect for self and others.
Fundamental to responsible thinking, decision making, and the development of relationships and communities within and across contexts, cultures, channels, and media.

terms.term: The 4 Principles of Communication Ethics by the NCA
answers: Advocate truthfulness, accuracy, honesty, and reason
Freedom of expression, diversity of perspective, and tolerance of dissent
Condemn communication that degrades individuals and humanity
Accept responsibility for the consequences of our own communication

sets.name: Communication Models
sets.description: The classic models of communication and White's stages of oral communication.

terms.term: 5 Elements of Aristotle's Model of Communication
8 Stages of White's Model of Oral Communication

sets.name: Public Speaking
sets.description: The nature and history of public speaking, its key figures, and Philippine traditions.

terms.definition: A process of communicating purposeful information in front of an audience. It is usually face-to-face and in a formal setting where the aim of the speaker is to influence the listeners.

terms.term: 5 Periods in the History of Public Speaking

terms.definition: The Greek teacher of rhetoric who, with his student Tisias, helped citizens speak persuasively in courts of law. According to him, a basic speech has three parts, and this simple organization has endured throughout the ages.

terms.term: 3 Parts of a Basic Speech according to Corax

terms.definition: The father of debate, who made his students argue for and against issues of the day, to sharpen their reasoning skills and appreciate different sides of an issue.
Also known as the father of modern communication; wrote a treatise entitled “Rhetoric,” where he discussed the use of logos, pathos, and ethos in persuasive speaking.
Refers to ethics, meaning a speaker must radiate moral character to create an aura of trust and authority in the audience; the speaker's character and credibility.

Means supporting your speech with logical reasoning in the form of facts, figures, and evidence, and one of the most effective ways of helping the audience get to the conclusion of an argument on their own.
Refers to adding an emotional touch to your speech, so as to cater to the audience's emotions.

terms.term: 3 Modes of Persuasion discussed by Aristotle

terms.definition: The most famous orator in Ancient Greece. In the beginning he had many flaws in public speaking, chief among them his stammer and weak voice; he practiced earnestly by declaiming on the seashore with pebbles in his mouth, and his speeches were known for their deliberation and forethought.

The most famous Roman orator, whose eloquence was described as a “resistless torrent.” A statesman who argued that the teaching of rhetoric should be considered an art form useful in all practical and public affairs, and who developed the Five Canons of Rhetoric.
The Roman lawyer and educator who forwarded the idea that public speakers should be ethical; he described the ideal speaker as “a good man speaking well.”
A Christian clergyman and renowned rhetorician who continued to develop ideas and study the persuasion that had originated during the Classical Period.
Challenged the theories of the great scholars from the Classical Period and focused on logic rather than rhetoric; according to him, logic falls under two parts.

terms.term: 2 Parts of Logic according to Petrus Ramus

terms.definition: A Scottish minister and educator who used scientific and moral reasoning to understand how persuasion in speech works.
An approach that mainly focused on the delivery aspect of public speaking, namely tone of voice, gestures, body language, facial expressions, and pronunciations.
Considered public speaking as a separate field of study; communication departments have professors or instructors to teach about classical and modern rhetoric.
A training organization that aims at teaching its members public speaking skills.

In pre-colonial times, women who were allowed to speak in public for the purpose of presiding over religious rituals; along with the warriors of the community, they were the leaders of pre-colonial Philippines.
The warriors of the community who, along with the babaylans, were the leaders of pre-colonial Philippines.
A game wherein young men and women duel with each other using words when it comes to talking about love.

A poetic joust staged to honor Francisco Balagtas; like an ordinary debate except that one has to reason and argue in verse, with two master poets defending the pros and cons of an issue and a board of judges determining the winner.
A game used to entertain guests and the bereaved family during wakes.

sets.name: Commentary
sets.description: Tour commentary: its types, components, audience analysis, and delivery.

terms.definition: Also known as “guidespeak”; a narrative used by a tour guide to describe a site and provide information about various aspects of a country to tourists while on tour. It covers the features and history of the location, and the tours can be from as little as 10-15 minutes to extended periods over many days.

terms.term: The 4 Basic Information About a Place to Include
The 13 Basic Facts About a Place
answers: Land area and distance from the city center

terms.term: The 5 Skills Required for Commentary Making
The 4 Types of Commentary Based on Necessity

terms.definition: Type of commentary that is essential information which must be delivered. The name of the tour guide, driver, or coordinator should be part of the introduction and greeting.
Type of commentary that includes all the basic details given, including the history, facts, and figures, whether on a running tour.
Type of commentary where, through interactive guiding, guests ask questions, and the tour guide is duty-bound to answer the information asked for clarification.
